item.title: Re: mysterious blackmail
item.content:encoded:
do you think I should get rid of the negative feelings thing?

Yes. In my response above, the paragraph starting with "So far as content goes, I'm not a fan of the premise since it relies heavily on a compulsion effect" covers why I don't think that effect helps your piece.

hey can you check if there is anything else I could delete there is the possible cause the materialization of the envelope

I'll be honest, right now it looks like you're focusing on the smaller details that don't really matter than much (envelope materialization) without addressing the bigger issues that are the more major roadblock to your concept being workable.

So far the revisions don't really address what I mentioned previously; in fact the premise is worse than the previous iteration because you've introduced more severe and overpowered effects that don't make sense. It's still unclear why the blackmail setup operates the way it does (did you take into account fraudulent charities? Redundant charities? Legitimate charities with leaders who embezzle money?). Additionally, the anomaly forcing people to give up what they have to the point where they beg for money and steal items to donate causes more problems, which ironically many charities try to prevent.

I think you might want to take a break from this idea for a little while and come back to it with fresh eyes. The recent edits you've made admittedly seem haphazard and not well thought-out.

Also, out of curiosity, have you read many Series V and Series VI SCP articles? The approach you're using here looks like it takes inspiration from Series I articles, which aren't usually the best example of current site expectations for quality and content.

item.title: Re: mysterious blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. As a general note, your concept post has a lot of simple errors like missing punctuation and run-on sentences. This automatically makes me as a reviewer hesitant to want to give a greenlight, as I am uncertain as to whether the draft would be written to the expected clinical tone standards for the mainsite.

+ show block
– hide block

So far as content goes, I'm not a fan of the premise since it relies heavily on a compulsion effect, which is one of the oldest anomalous shortcuts on the site. As a general note, the "it makes you crazy/act a very specific way" approach isn't particularly interesting on its own anymore, given how many times SCPs with that effect have been written. Take a look at the articles tagged with "compulsion". Typically, an SCP object's effect forcing someone to do something tends to come off as a lazy or contrived narrative, since there's more genuine tension if there's a struggle involved, and/or if the people instead act of their own volition rather than just because the author needs them to for the story to work. Consider reading through the further discussion on the narrative issues of compulsion and addiction effects.

The details about the anomaly are also kind of strange. The phrasing of "all sentient organisms", for example. Dogs, cats, and even lobsters are considered sentient. I presume none of them can donate though? Also, the "go to your nearest charity" bit doesn't quite make sense since not all charity organizations have easily accessible buildings (some charities set up donation drop boxes for things like used clothes and toys, and others have someone with a desk and box sitting in front of a grocery store). The fact that the type of money rarely changes implies that the anomaly is solely affecting countries that use the US dollar/people who have access to US money. Why? In general, the details surrounding the setup seem rather random, rather than supported by an in-universe reason.

Overall though… my main question here is "why does this happen?" The anomalous blackmail is creepy, sure, but to someone who can spare $10 and the time/energy to make a trip to drop if off, this is just a weird, potentially annoying detour in their regular daily life. The threatening note about the coma just feels, again, predictable: SCPs don't need to be dangerous to be successful.

The hook of "the secret is mysterious" admittedly feels a little lazy to me. It also leads to the question, "what if someone doesn't have any secrets, or doesn't care if their secrets are revealed?"

I feel like for this to be workable, you'd need to do a lot of revisions. For me to be more likely to enjoy the premise, I'd need to know:

  • why is this blackmail scheme happening to begin with?
  • why does the blackmail scheme operate the way it does?
  • where does the money go?
  • how would the Foundation find out about the anomaly in the first place?

Ideally the answers to these questions would work well within the context of an overarching story, rather than just a collection of information bits thrown together conflictingly.

We definitely already have a lot of exchange-based articles on the site (you can use the Tag Search tool to find them). What will make yours unique and memorable?

item.title: Re: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Okay so I have two big concerns here. The first is that narratively, it feels like this is very similar to SCP-4645 in style; down to the like, random blackmail claims and the unclear like, requirement for what the foundation should do.

The second is that this doesn't really go anywhere: you introduce the mystery of who is sending this and that the blackmail changes repeatedly but it doesn't go anywhere. Like, the foundation doesn't investigate who sent it, they don't really debate whether to accede to the demands, they don't refuse and have progressively worse things happen; so it just feels very…flat?

My advice: figure out how you can show why this is interesting. Figure out what the narrative arc of this is.

item.title: blackmail for charity
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Mystery

Page Layout: Scp article with story elements

Elevator Pitch

  • Black envelope containing blackmail listing demands by the threat of making mankind suffer.
  • Envelope has a 10-meter radius of effect making all humans have a sense of empathy to charities followed by the affected individuals repeating the phrase: Destroy the sins of Mankind to clean the world of its filth for 30 minutes followed by them donating all of their belongings to charities.
  • The blackmail dematerializes and materializes each month=Blackmail event
+ show block
– hide block

central narrative:

The Discovery of this envelope was made: A sudden electrical surge causes static to the surveillance cameras in a break room, After this event, a series of 26 separate cases of Foundation personnel started taking an interest in donating to charities with each case being in the same break room after the electrical surge shortly after a camera check it was discovered the envelope was the cause of this phenomenon.
The following message was in the envelope: inspection via a mechanical arm

Thank you kind soul for Believing that there is a way of destroying the corruption and evil in our cruel world remember that every dollar given is 1 life saved. - [[unillegible]]
Every person I have seen doesn't believe in the ideas of freedom a with this in mind though I will rather believe humanity has a chance for redemption so donate $10,000 US or the world will suffer more from their own flaws you have 1 month to meet my demands.

When the demand is not met on time a series of events will happen that will directly inflict damage to the economy to the state with the most failed charities till the demand is met.

address to charity: Charity in need

charityEvent#moc.liamg|3#moc.liamg|3

Hook/Attention Grabber: The mystery to the envelope and the relation to charities.

Additional Notes: Discovery of the envelope was made after a series of charities in America shown to be hoaxes.

The blackmail demands changes correlate with the country with the most unsuccessful charities in the world with kind used in that country is used for the demand at the beginning of each month.

When individuals affected by this envelope run out of belongings they begin to beg for money if they are not given money frequently they begin to steal any objects to donate.

When an individual goes to their nearest charity with financial issues and donates the currency listed on the demand the currency undergoes rapid combustion until there are no traces of the money left.
